- Practice:  Build a gateway that routes simple queries to a quantized local model and complex reasoning to a frontier API based on prompt complexity.

Meta put out a deep dive today on “Prometheus”, its gigawatt-scale training cluster in New Albany, Ohio, and it's a great example of co-engineering to the max with @nvidia. Meta says it goes beyond a normal vendor relationship with teams embedded in the data centers, sharing real-time telemetry and running joint triage on every halt.

Hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs across multiple buildings today, roughly 1M at full scale, and phase one trained the @Muse models. I got an early read over the weekend. What I liked most is Meta put real failure data out there. You don't see that very often. 

Here are the deets:
•in mid-2025, Meta was seeing nearly 1,000 interruptions per 8K GPUs per DAY. Down 99% since.
•the goal is 2 per 8K GPUs a day, so by my math they're still about 5x off.
•each 72-GPU rack runs a 64-GPU job slice because training likes powers of two. The other 8 are hot spares, plus ~2% extra racks. Roughly 1 in 8 GPUs in a big run sits in reserve.
•GB300 was 5-10% faster than GB200 for Meta. Looks like Meta pulled 800G per GPU forward on its GB200s, so it didn't get that bump. Meta expects Vera Rubin to add 10-20% perf/watt.
•Arista chassis on Broadcom Jericho3 connect buildings anywhere from 2 km to 100+ km apart.
•starting or pausing one big job can swing tens of megawatts in seconds.

At this scale you're fighting reliability and power every day, and that co-engineering matters as much as the chips.

Good fodder ahead of Meta earnings Wednesday.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

16日の米国株式市場で、AIクラウド新興企業のコアウィーブの株価が再び急落しました。
一時14%安となり、終値でも12%安でした。

巨額の投資を借金に頼る新興企業が売られる一方、お金に余裕のある巨大テック企業の株は底堅く、同じAI関連株の中でも財務の強さで選別が進んでいます📉

—

💡 新興AIクラウド株の下落が広がる

・コアウィーブ株は16日に一時14%安、終値で12%安
・15日はエヌビディアのジェンスン・ファンCEOが｢コアウィーブの財務に楽観的だ｣と語って急反発したが、効果は続かなかった
・エヌビディアはコアウィーブの大株主で、GPU(画像処理半導体)の供給元でもある
・ナスダック総合指数は16日に2%強下げ、1カ月ぶりの安値水準
・豪IRENは16日に11%安となり、9月末より3割強安い水準
・オランダのネビウス・グループや米アプライド・デジタルも9月末から3割弱下落
・一方でマイクロソフトは3%高、アマゾン・ドット・コムも小幅高

→同じAI関連でも、新興勢と巨大テックで株価の動きが分かれています✋️

—

💡 借金頼みの財務が重荷に

・AIクラウド事業者が顧客に計算能力を提供するには、GPUの大量確保など巨額のお金が必要
・マイクロソフトなどの巨大テックは、ほかの事業で稼いだ現金をAI投資に回せる
・｢ネオクラウド｣と呼ばれる新興AIクラウド事業者は、借金への依存が強まっている
・金利が上がる中で、これまで見過ごされてきた借金のコストの重さが改めて意識されている

→資金力の差が、株価の明暗を分けています✋️

—

💡 財務の数字で見ても差は大きい

・ICR(インタレスト・カバレッジ・レシオ)は、本業の利益で借金の利息を何倍払えるかを示す指標
・新興勢のICRは軒並み1倍未満で、IRENは0.1倍と、本業の利益だけでは利息を払いきれない状態
・マイクロソフトのICRは100倍超
・ネットDEレシオ(実質的な借金が自己資本の何倍あるか)は、コアウィーブが7倍超、オラクルも3倍と高い
・こうした会社は、金利上昇で利息の負担が増えたり、お金を借りにくくなったりすると影響を受けやすい

→借金の多い会社ほど、金利上昇に弱い形になっています✋️

—

💡 AI需要の伸びにも変化の兆し

・米英メディアによると、アンソロピックの26年7〜9月期売上高は前の四半期比45%増の168億ドル(約2兆6000億円)
・2倍超の伸びだった4〜6月期からは減速
・AI開発企業の成長が鈍ると、クラウド事業の投資回収にも影響が出る
・BofAによると、米巨大テック5社の27年の設備投資予想は今年に入って8割上方修正された一方、AI関連の売上高予想の引き上げは2割にとどまる

→投資の増え方に、売り上げの増え方が追いついていない状況です✋️

—

💡 株安は行き過ぎとの見方も

・エバコアISIのアナリストは｢事業モデルが機能しなくなったとみるべきではない｣と主張
・コアウィーブは1040億ドルの受注残を抱えている
・事業の採算性は損なわれていないとの見方

→売られすぎとみる声もあります✋️

—

🎏 総評まとめ

コアウィーブなど借金に頼ってAI投資を進める新興企業の株が売られ、お金に余裕のある巨大テックとの差がはっきりしてきました📉

AIへの期待が高い間は、借金の重さはあまり気にされていませんでした。

しかし金利が上がって利息の負担が意識されるようになり、投資家は会社の｢財務の強さ｣を厳しく見るようになっています。

さらに、巨大テックの設備投資の見通しが大きく増える一方で、AIの売り上げの見通しはそれほど増えていません。

投資したお金を本当に回収できるのか、という疑問が出てきたことも売りにつながっていそうです。

ただ、コアウィーブは1040億ドルもの受注残を抱えており、事業そのものがだめになったわけではありません。

同じ｢AI銘柄｣でも、これからは夢の大きさより借金と利益のバランスで選ばれる時代に入ったのかもしれませんね🎏💭

市場では、10月の日銀会合では金利を据え置き、その次の12月の日銀会合で追加利上げに踏み切るかが注目されています📈

—

💡 物価は日銀の｢2%目標｣にほぼ届いている

・日銀が重視する物価の基本的な流れ(基調的な物価上昇率)について、植田総裁は｢2%におおむね近い｣と説明

・9月の利上げ後も、お金を借りやすい｢緩和的｣な状態が続いていると指摘
・｢引き続き政策金利を引き上げて緩和度合いを調整していく｣との考えを示した

→物価の上がりすぎを防ぐため、利上げを続ける姿勢をはっきり示しました✋️

—

💡 物価を押し上げる3つのリスクに注目

・日銀は、インフレを強めるリスクとして次の3点を挙げている
・1つ目は、中東情勢の緊迫による原油高
・2つ目は、AI関連の需要の拡大
・3つ目は、円安
・植田総裁は、この3点を引き続き注意して見ていく考えを改めて示した
・9月の日銀会合後の日本経済のデータは、おおむね日銀の見通しどおりに動いていると説明

→今のところ景気や物価は日銀の想定に沿っており、見通しを変えるほどの材料はないとの見方です✋️

—

💡 海外の金融当局との意見交換

・G20会議などで、世界の金融政策の担当者と議論
・｢AI関連需要は日銀が見ているよりもややしっかりしている｣と考える人が多かったと振り返った
・米連邦準備理事会(FRB)のウォーシュ議長とは｢様々な意見交換をした｣と説明(具体的な内容には触れず)
・8月に米国でベッセント米財務長官と面会して以降は｢特にコミュニケーションはとっていない｣と明言

→海外ではAI需要の強さを日銀より高く見る声が多く、物価を押し上げる要因として意識されています✋️

—

💡 次の利上げのタイミングが焦点

・日銀は9月の日銀会合で政策金利を0.25%引き上げ、1.25%にした
・次回の日銀会合は10月29〜30日に開かれる
・市場では10月は据え置き、12月に追加利上げするかが焦点との見方が多い
・景気を熱しも冷ましもしない金利の水準(中立金利)については｢はっきりこの辺にあると言える材料はない｣と説明
・｢これまでの利上げの累積的効果が出ているかを見ながら判断したい｣とも述べた

→どこまで金利を上げるかは、これまでの利上げの効き目を確かめながら決めていく方針です✋️

—

🎏 総評まとめ

植田総裁の発言からは、物価の上がりすぎを防ぐために日銀が利上げを続けていく強い姿勢が伝わってきます📈

9月に政策金利を1.25%まで引き上げた後も、お金を借りやすい状態はまだ続いているため、日銀は利上げを続ける余地があると考えています。

一方で、どこまで金利を上げれば景気を熱しも冷ましもしない水準になるのかは、日銀自身もはっきりとは分かっていません。

原油高やAI需要の広がり、円安といった物価を押し上げる要因が続くなかで、12月の日銀会合で追加利上げがあるかが今後の注目点になります。

物価の上昇をこれ以上は認めないとまで言い切ったのはかなり強いメッセージで、12月の追加利上げが一気に現実味を帯びてきた印象ですね🎏💭

$PRME | Prime editing turns routine immunosuppressants into an on-off switch for engineered T cells

Published today in Blood: a WEHI-led team in Australia has built a prime editing platform designed so clinicians can control therapeutic T cells using drugs already stocked in hospital pharmacies.

Patients who need ongoing immunosuppression, including people with rare immune disorders, organ and stem cell transplant recipients, and some cancer patients, take drugs that suppress the engineered cells along with everything else. Once the cells are back in the body, clinicians have few ways to selectively support or restrain them.

The team edited T cells to be resistant to tacrolimus while keeping them sensitive to cyclosporin, a closely related alternative. One drug lets the edited cells survive while the surrounding immune system stays suppressed. The other remains available to shut the edited cells down if they behave unexpectedly.

Three design constraints, stated by the group: the selecting drug had to be one clinicians already prescribe and know how to manage, the resistance had to come from rewriting single letters in the cell's own genes rather than inserting new genetic material, and the edited genes could not be linked to cancer.

The work used cells from patients with SPTCL-HLH, a rare and serious immune-related blood cancer that can affect children and young adults. Prime editing was applied twice in the same cells: once to correct the disease-causing mutation, once to install tacrolimus resistance. The same platform was then tested in virus-specific T cells, aimed at helping transplant recipients fight infection without stopping anti-rejection drugs, and in CAR T cells. The team is now working toward a first-in-human trial.

The group's stated longer-term goal, not demonstrated in this paper, is extending the approach to blood stem cells across the 600-plus inherited blood and immune disorders, so corrected cells could be expanded with a tablet instead of chemotherapy conditioning.

Prime editing was developed in David Liu's lab and is in-licensed by Prime Medicine from the Broad Institute, under a licence limited to the prevention or treatment of human disease. Multiplex editing in T cells, correcting a pathogenic variant and installing a separate functional edit in the same cell without cutting both DNA strands, is the specific capability Prime supplies to Bristol Myers Squibb under their 2024 ex vivo T-cell collaboration. Prime also generated the first clinical data for prime editing in humans with PM359 in chronic granulomatous disease.

Quantinuum announced a quantum error-correction record on Monday. It is a great result, but in my view it does not bring a CRQC / Q-Day any closer. Despite what some comments and media proclaim.

On its Helios machine, the team protected one logical qubit, built from 73 physical qubits, through repeated rounds of error checking. It failed about five times per million rounds. Each time the team enlarged the code, the error rate fell about twelvefold on average. On Google's Willow chip in 2024, the error rate fell about twofold per step.

With errors falling that fast, a trapped-ion machine would need far fewer physical qubits for each error-corrected qubit. By my arithmetic, each logical qubit would need about 660 physical qubits in Quantinuum's layout to fail only once in a trillion rounds, roughly twelve times fewer than at Willow's 2024 rate.

Each round of error correction on Helios takes about a fifth of a second, against 1.1 microseconds on Willow. IonQ estimated last month that 19,397 trapped ions could recover one Bitcoin private key in about 26 days per attempt, assuming 200-microsecond operations. Rescaled to the speed of Helios's gates today, each attempt would take about 12 years. To finish an attack in weeks, a trapped-ion machine would need operations more than a hundred times faster than Helios's.

After this paper, I would lower the qubit estimate for a trapped-ion attack and leave the time estimate where it was.

Contrarian Thinking.

Over and over the contrarians are the ones who change the world. But it is a muscle that needs constant exercise. The masses have the market share and most people hate change.

"I would never share my house with others." AirBnb was born.

"I would never use a digital camera," I heard at Eastman Kodak's booth years ago. Today I shoot all my photos on iPhone.

"I love to drive." Today I often take a Waymo.

"Babies use mice and GUIs." I heard that one in college from a Unix programmer. Now we are headed into a world where we don't use mice and GUIs, thanks to voice systems and brain computer interface companies.

"Art can't be done with AI." Now when you are the Sphere in Las Vegas you are watching a movie dramatically improved with AI.

"Our customers love buttons," engineers at Mercedes Benz said, while pointing out to me that touching screens is more dangerous while driving than touching buttons.

"Cooking with microwaves isn't as good as using an open flame," many chefs have told me. Yet when you arrive home late and need to make something for the kids do you listen to the chefs?

"I'll never use a phone without a physical keyboard," many told me. Yet here we are.

"I'll never use an autofocus camera," many pro photographers told me. Now it is weird if you see a pro manually focusing. 

So, how can you build your contrarian muscle?

Go back to the core problem that humans are trying to solve and rethink it without bias. 

On Friday @broodsugar told the audience at @TheHumanoidHub's event that a Chinese retailer asked themselves "what if humans actually suck at running a retailer." They automated every decision. AI manages every store. Makes every decision of where to put products, and how many to stock, that kind of thing. Sales went up 258%. And this was a well established retailer with billions in sales every year. 

Other ways I was able to get ahead of everyone when I wrote my eight books (I wrote a book about social media before Twitter started). 

1. Learn about bleeding edge tech and ask yourself "what if this got adopted?"

2. Hang around with others who have demonstrated contrarian thinking. 

3. Dream about what the world would look like if your new thing actually worked for everyone. Would the world improve or get worse?

4. Learn some secrets that very few others know. I once talked at Google's first advertiser's conference and they sat me at a VIP table with Kraft food execs. They told me why they advertise and told me how much they spend to acquire a new customer. $34. So when Instagram was bought by Mark Zuckerberg I knew it was an amazing purchase, since Instagram's users were growing exponentially every few weeks. I gave a speech to billionaires that morning who thought it was the stupidest purchase they ever had heard of. It had no sales. No profits. 14 employees. No assets. That is consensus thinking. Which they got into because that's how businesses were (and still are) measured. 

5. Study the problems that people actually are having and then find new ways to solve those problems with fresh eyes. Heck, you can see this in action by visiting @reservoirfarms, that has 20 new companies building farming robots. Every entrepreneur I talked with there spent years walking in farms with farmers, understanding their problems, before they started building robots. I have met many entrepreneurs who worked in weird jobs to learn the industry they are going after. Have you worked on a manufacturing line? In a dentist's office? Or, done landscaping? "First principles" applies to every human endeavor.

6. Learn from Eric Reis. When he was building one of his first companies he spent months building software that he thought people would want. When he launched it no one visited his home page. He learned to test his weird ideas first before he built another thing. 

7. Hang out with people who are different. Years ago I got to hang out with Steve Mann. I shot this photo in 2014, and he had already worn a device on his face for 20 years, even had a screw implanted in his skull so that he could more easily wear a wearable computer. He was weird, let's be honest. Never met someone like him before. But ask yourself "what if he is right, and everyone else is wrong?" There are armies who will tell you they never will wear smart glasses, even today. Can you resist armies who will give you every reason why they never will do the new weird thing?

8. Hang out with the young. I remember being in Hyde Jr. High's first computer club in Cupertino back in 1977. Only five people in it. There were armies of older people (and even many other kids) who would tell me they never would use one and had no need for it. I hung out with @photomatt in San Francisco 20 years ago when he was only 17, and hearing his dreams of how people and companies would publish in the future radically changed my life for the past 20 years. Same for interviewing @VitalikButerin when he was about that age. Laid out an entirely new economics system based on smart contracts. Mullenweg had just started his company and saw a new way for humans to communicate. Today, what, 80% of the Web is running on his software, Wordpress. As much as I hate it, it is rare that people my age (I'm now almost 62) comes up with such a radical shift. It does happen, but far more likely that a 17 year old is gonna build a dramatically important company than I am. Why? They are not burdened by "the way things are done."

9. Ask yourself "is there a better way to do this?" Steve Jobs told his original iPhone team not to hire anyone who worked on a phone at any other company. He didn't want to hear why something wouldn't work, he wanted fresh thinking and new ideas. Back to getting rid of buttons.

10. Question your own assumptions. They might be completely wrong. Mine often are. And be OK with that. I once said that I would wear a Google Glass the rest of my life. That was wrong, obviously. Sometimes I talk myself into points of view that don't turn out to be right. At least short term. (I still am looking for a pair that will make that a right statement). 

11. Build and test with humans who won't blow smoke up your ass (not your friends and family). 

12. Read a lot of books. Anyone who writes a book has thought a LOT about what they are presenting. They often see cracks in consensus thinking. Yeah, often they are science fiction authors, but often not. (I have to take that advice more myself, dropped off my reading). Especially true regarding people who write about new ideas and how to put them into use in business (same here on X, which is why if I find a contrarian thinker I put them on my lists).

13. Remember "experts" are people who got good at building for the masses. But they often have deep blind spots on where the future will be and they often will give you bad advice. 

14. Ask yourself "what if everyone had an autonomous car, a VR headset, a robot, a brain computer interface?" What would be needed that doesn't exist in such a world? 

15. Question your world view. I once was highly religious, went to church three times on Sunday. Thought I was right back then too. And religion is still the dominant world view most people have, but it isn't the only one. Ask most people about autonomous cars and you'll hear religion come back "I'll never let the government look at me while I drive." That's a belief system that person is locked into. 

16. Ask yourself "how could I change even the worst hater?" One "secret" I learned over and over in my career is people change, and even give up religious belief systems, when presented with something new. Henry Ford used to say "if I asked people what they wanted, they answered 'a better horse.'" They couldn't dream of a contraption that would drive them around. Even last night I talked with a Stanford Fellow who gave me the same answer about autonomous cars. He used to run California Microwave, is a very smart guy, but used to have a race car and is stuck in the world view of "I love to drive." 

I could go for quite a while longer, but wanted to open it up to you. 

How do you put contrarian thinking into use in your own life/business or in the things you are building? Are you starting a contarian company? One that, if successful, will force everyone to change? 

This post due to Brendan Footy, @BrendanFoody cofounder of Mercor, who shared this post this morning: https://t.co/jcDgICpl4m

DARPA’s N³ program was not about vague futuristic speculation. It was an official U.S. defense research program focused on building a high-performance, bi-directional brain-machine interface.

N³ stands for Next-Generation Nonsurgical Neurotechnology.

According to DARPA’s own program description, the goal was to create a system that could read from and write to 16 independent channels within a 16 mm³ volume of neural tissue within 50 milliseconds. DARPA also said each channel was intended to interact with sub-millimeter regions of the brain with timing and precision approaching more invasive systems.

The goal was not just passive brain monitoring. The program was explicitly framed around two-way communication between brain tissue and machines.

DARPA’s 2018 announcement explained the purpose even more plainly. The agency said N³ was created to pursue a safe, portable neural interface system capable of reading from and writing to multiple points in the brain at once. The program was aimed at future military applications involving human-machine teaming, including potential interaction with unmanned aerial vehicles and active cyber defense systems.

Another important detail...

This was designed for able-bodied service members, not only for medical therapy. That tells you the conversation goes beyond restoring lost function. It also includes expanding direct communication between human brains and digital systems in operational environments.

DARPA also made clear that the program was trying to do this without surgery, which is what made N³ different from older invasive brain-computer interface approaches.

So when people act like two-way brain interfaces are still just sci-fi, they’re ignoring what has already been publicly stated by DARPA.

How far did the program get?

What technologies came out of it?

What follow-on programs are building on that work?

And how should the public think about privacy, autonomy, and consent as these systems keep advancing?

米国の物価上昇の勢いが強まっています📈

米労働統計局(BLS)が14日に発表した9月の消費者物価指数(CPI)は前年同月比3.7%上昇し、8月の3.4%から伸びが大きくなりました。
ガソリンの値上がりが物価全体を強く押し上げています📈

—

💡 物価全体の伸びが拡大

・9月の消費者物価指数(CPI)は前年同月比3.7%上昇で、8月の3.4%から拡大
・前月比では0.6%上昇で、8月の0.4%から伸びが大きくなった
・前月比の上昇分のうち、半分以上はガソリンの値上がりによるもの

→ガソリン高が、物価全体を押し上げる一番の要因になっています✋️

—

💡 エネルギー価格が大きく上昇

・ガソリンは前月比9.1%上昇、前年同月比では34.2%上昇
・エネルギー全体は前月比5.2%上昇で、8月の2.1%から加速
・エネルギー全体の前年同月比は20.4%上昇
・暖房などに使う燃料油は、前年同月比74.2%上昇
・電気代は前年同月比4.4%、都市ガス代は5.0%上昇

→エネルギー価格は1年前と比べて2割も高くなっています✋️

—

💡 ガソリン高の背景は中東での攻撃激化

・9月は中東で石油施設やタンカーへの攻撃が増え、原油価格が上昇
・特に、ホルムズ海峡を通らずに原油を運べるサウジアラビアの東西パイプラインが攻撃を受け、輸送が一時止まった
・このパイプラインは攻撃前、1日500万バレル超の原油を輸出に回していたと米エネルギー情報局(EIA)は推計
・ロシアのエネルギー施設への攻撃も、原油の供給不安を強めた
・国際的な原油の指標であるブレント原油の9月の平均価格は1バレル114ドルで、8月より23ドル高い
・9月15日には一時1バレル131ドルまで上昇
・米国のレギュラーガソリンの平均価格は、8月31日の1ガロン(約3.8リットル)4.07ドルから、9月21日には4.48ドルまで上昇

→原油の輸送ルートが狙われたことで原油が値上がりし、ガソリンの値段も押し上げられました✋️

—

💡 コア指数の伸びもやや拡大

・物価の基本的な流れを見るうえで注目される、食品とエネルギーを除いたコア指数は前年同月比2.6%上昇
・8月の2.4%から伸びが大きくなった
・前月比では0.3%上昇で、8月と同じペース
・家賃などの住居費は前月比0.4%上昇、前年同月比3.2%上昇
・航空運賃は前月比1.2%上昇、前年同月比では22.4%上昇
・中古車は前月比0.7%上昇
・一方で、処方薬は前月比1.2%下落、通信費は0.2%下落

→燃料の値上がりが航空運賃などにも広がり、コア指数を少しずつ押し上げています✋️

—

💡 食品価格は落ち着いた動き

・食品全体は前月比で横ばい、前年同月比2.5%上昇
・スーパーなどで買う食品は前月比0.1%下落
・牛肉は前月比1.0%下落、牛乳は2.0%下落
・外食は前月比0.2%上昇、前年同月比3.5%上昇

→エネルギーとは違い、食品の値上がりは一服しています✋️

—

💡 FRBの追加利上げは12月との見方

・FRBは9月の会合で、3年2カ月ぶりに利上げを決めた
・次回のFOMCは10月27〜28日で、その次は12月8〜9日
・金利先物の値動きから見た市場予想では、年内に0.25%の追加利上げが1回あるとの見方が7割
・一方で、10月の会合での利上げ予想は2割にとどまる

→市場では｢10月は据え置き、12月に利上げ｣という見方が目立っています✋️

—

🎏 総評まとめ

9月の米国の消費者物価指数(CPI)は、ガソリンを中心としたエネルギー高で伸びが3.7%に拡大しました📈

前月比の上昇分の半分以上をガソリンが占めており、燃料価格の影響がとても大きい結果でした。

その背景には、中東で石油施設やタンカーへの攻撃が増え、原油の値段が大きく上がったことがあります。

食品とエネルギーを除いたコア指数も2.6%に伸びが大きくなり、航空運賃などを通じて燃料高がほかの値段にも広がり始めています。

一方で、食品の値段は前月から横ばいで、物価全体が一斉に上がっているわけではありません。

物価の伸びが強まったことで、FRBが次にいつ利上げするのかに注目が集まりそうです。

ガソリンが1年で3割以上も値上がりし、たった1カ月で9%も上がっているのは、車社会の米国にとってかなり痛い出費ですね🎏💭

・生産・仕入れから販売までの土台をそろえ、購買や決済も一本化してコストを下げる
・顧客データをまとめて、デジタルを使った販促を強化する
・ネットと店舗をつなげた売り方(OMO)や商品の相互供給、地方・海外での販売ルートの共同開発も進める
・浮いたお金はM&Aや海外展開、循環型ビジネス、人材への投資に回す
・統合後はTSI、ワールド・ブランズ、ワールド・ソリューションズの3社を中間持ち株会社にする

→｢守り｣のコスト削減と｢攻め｣の成長投資の両方を狙っています✋️

—

💡 業界3位とはいえ首位との差は大きい

・ワールドの26年2月期の売上収益は2840億円、営業利益は160億円
・TSIHDの26年2月期の売上高は1670億円、営業利益は43億円
・単純に合わせると売上高は4510億円で、ファーストリテイリング(3兆9633億円)、しまむら(7000億円)に次ぐ国内3位
・ただし、この数字には商社機能などアパレル以外の事業も含まれる
・TSIHDは11年に東京スタイルとサンエー・インターナショナルが統合して生まれた会社

→3位になっても、ファーストリテイリングとの売上の差は8倍以上あります✋️

—

🎏 総評まとめ

ワールドとTSIHDの経営統合は、国内アパレルが｢規模を大きくしてコストを下げる｣時代に入ったことを示す動きです📈

国内ではお店やブランドが多すぎる一方で、人口は減り、円安で仕入れコストも上がっています。

ファーストリテイリングの売上高は4兆円近くまで伸びており、中堅の企業が1社だけで戦うのは難しくなってきました。

ワールドは26年2月期にコロナ禍後で初めての減益となり、主力ブランドの立て直しが課題になっていました。

TSIHDも25年に｢フリークス ストア｣を運営するデイトナ・インターナショナルを283億円で買収するなど、規模の拡大を進めてきました。

実は25年3月には、TSIHDが縫製子会社をワールドに売却しており、両社はもともと取引のある間柄でした。

統合の効果が出るかどうかは、物流やシステムの一本化をどれだけ早く進められるかにかかっています。

｢アンタイトル｣と｢フリークス ストア｣が同じグループになるという組み合わせには正直驚きましたが、ブランドが重ならない2社だからこそ、ここからどんな新しい売り場が生まれるのか楽しみですね🎏💭
